ENV_AC_Unit.method:
Split air-conditioning outdoor unit on wall brackets, fan grille, refrigerant pipes in a white trunking:
the 21st-century addition every Spanish facade has somewhere (owner: "falta arquitectura contemporánea").

ENV_AFrame_Board.method: Bar A-frame chalkboard (pizarra): two timber-framed boards leaning together, the chalk face maps a notice.

ENV_ATM.method: Cash machine set in a bank's ground floor: stainless surround, hood, screen, keypad, card and cash slots.

ENV_Alarm_Box.method: Burglar-alarm siren box over a shop: white case, coloured flash lens.

ENV_Awning.method:
Shop awning (toldo) over a 2 m bay: striped canvas on a gentle convex curve, scalloped valance, iron arms and
front bar. The canvas slot (ENV_Canvas_*) carries the stripes; one texture tile across the bay = 4 stripes.

ENV_Balcony_Iron.method:
Shallow stone-slab balcony with a wrought-iron railing and two iron brackets (balconera).
Slab on the kit MI_RockTrim slab band; ironwork is owned flat iron.

ENV_Bell.method: Bronze bell with yoke for the belfry openings.

ENV_Bench_Stone.method: Stone bench (poyo) against a wall or around a tree: two blocks and a thick slab.

ENV_Bench_Street.method: Municipal street bench: cast-iron ends, timber slats (kit MI_WoodTrim dark band), faces +z.

ENV_Bicycle.method: Ordinary town bicycle, 1.7 m, wheels in the y-z plane (length along z); frame paint slot ENV_Paint_Red.

ENV_Bike_Rack.method: Three galvanised hoops set in the paving.

ENV_Bin_Street.method:
Rustic litter bin: ring of dark timber slats (kit MI_WoodTrim dark band) bound by two iron hoops, iron rim,
dark liner inside. Free-standing, 0.8 m.

ENV_Blade_Sign.method:
Projecting light-box sign (modern shops, pharmacy cross): steel arm and a 0.6 m square box, both faces carry
the sign texture (ENV_Sign_Board remapped per business).

ENV_Boat_Small.method:
Small inshore fishing boat (lancha), 5.6 m, bow towards +z, waterline at y = 0. Hull paint slot
ENV_Paint_Blue with a white sheer strake and a small wheelhouse.

ENV_Bollard_Mooring.method: Cast-iron mooring bollard (noray) for the quay coping: base plate, waisted body, mushroom cap.

ENV_Bollard_Street.method: Cast-iron street bollard (pilona), 0.95 m: moulded foot, slightly tapering body, collar and domed cap.

ENV_Box_Cardboard.method: Cardboard delivery box (0.5 x 0.4 x 0.35 m).

ENV_Bridge_Arch.method:
Stone arch under a casco bridge, as a 1 m wide slice along z that the district builder scales to the deck
width and along x to the span: segmental arch (span 10 m, springing 3.4 m below the deck, crown 0.6 m below it),
a ring of dressed voussoirs on both faces, rubble spandrels up to a moulded string course, rubble soffit.
Deck top at y = 0 (the builder lays the paved deck on it).

ENV_Cable_Run_2m.method: Surface-fixed service cable (2 m along the facade) with clips — added long after the building.

ENV_Chimney_Flue.method: Galvanised stove flue with a conical rain cap and a guy wire stub (a later addition on many roofs).

ENV_Chimney_Stone.method: Rendered/stone chimney stack with a projecting cap and two tiles laid as a little roof (casco chimney).

ENV_Clock_Face.method: Tower clock: 1.3 m white enamel dial in a stone ring, twelve iron hour marks and two hands (at 10 past 4).

ENV_Clothesline.method:
Window clothesline (tendedero): two iron brackets 0.55 m out from the wall, two lines, hanging clothes
in several colours. Mounted under an upper-floor window (origin on the wall face at bracket height).

ENV_Corner_Column.method: Cast-iron corner column (3 m) carrying the corner above a chamfered ground-floor entrance.

ENV_Counter_Shop.method: Shop counter 1.8 x 0.6 x 0.95 m: painted timber front panels, stone-slab top.

ENV_Crate_Fish.method: Stackable plastic fish crate (0.6 x 0.4 x 0.22 m) with hand holes; colour is a material slot.

ENV_Door_Balcony.method:
Glazed double balcony door (balconera / ventanal) for the kit Door_Flat wall opening: two leaves with kick
panels and 2x3 panes. Replaces the kit's plank doors on upper floors. Kit MI_WoodTrim + MI_WindowGlass.

ENV_Door_Portal_Reformed.method:
1980s replacement portal door for the kit Door_Flat opening: bronze-anodised aluminium frame, wired glass,
push bar. Joinery slot is palette-remapped like painted timber.

ENV_Door_Service.method: Plain galvanised service door for the kit Door_Flat wall opening (1.3 m): reads as back-of-house, not public.

ENV_Door_Step.method: Worn granite door step (umbral) 1.3 m, 15 cm: the portal meets the street on a stone, not on the paving.

ENV_Downpipe.method:
Rain-water downpipe, 3 m per unit height (the assembler scales y by storeys): painted iron pipe with socket
collars and wall brackets. Hopper head and shoe are separate modules so scaling never stretches them.

ENV_Downpipe_Head.method:
Hopper head (embudo) under the eave: flared box collecting the gutter, short neck into the pipe. Pipe top at
y = 0; the hopper sits above it.

ENV_Downpipe_Shoe.method: Pipe shoe (zapata): the pipe kicks forward at the foot and ends in a cast-iron boot over the channel.

ENV_Drain_Grate.method: Cast-iron gutter grate set in the carriageway beside the kerb.

ENV_Drain_Outlet.method: Drain outlet through the river wall: iron pipe mouth with a lip, a little stone apron under it.

ENV_Eave_Canecillos.method:
Lebaniego deep eave for one 2 m bay, fitted under the kit roof overhang: timber boarding (tablazón) following
the roof underside, five carved rafter tails (canecillos) and the wall plate. y = 0 is the facade top (floors x
3 m), the street face is at z = WALL_FACE. Kit MI_WoodTrim trim sheet (palette joinery: chestnut).

ENV_Escudo.method:
Generic casona shield (escudo) in sandstone, 0.7 x 1.0 m: moulded cartouche, heater-shaped field with a plain
cross-quartering, crest scroll on top and a corbel below. Heraldry-neutral: no real family arms.

ENV_Extractor_Vent.method: Kitchen/bathroom extractor outlet: louvred plastic grille with a sooty drip below.

ENV_Fence_Yard_2m.method:
Controlled work-yard boundary, 2 m panel x 2.1 m: galvanised palisade on a low plinth. Distinct from the
public quay railing by height, material and permeability (you see through, you cannot pass).

ENV_Fountain_Monument.method:
The plaza's landmark (owner: "algo que haga que el jugador diga: estoy aquí"): a granite octagonal basin on
two steps, a fluted central pier with four bronze spouts and, on top, a cast-iron five-lantern candelabra that
lights the plaza at night. ~9 m across the steps, 7.5 m high. Invented; no real monument copied.

ENV_Fountain_Trough.method:
Village fountain and trough (fuente-abrevadero): dressed stone pillar with a moulded cap and an iron spout, a
long stone trough with water, a step. Back against a wall at z = 0, facing +z.

ENV_Gallery_Bay.method:
Glazed gallery bay (galería/mirador) for one 2 m bay and one storey, projecting 0.55 m: timber base panel,
3x3 glazing grid, cornice and a small lead-grey cap. Stacks storey on storey. Kit MI_WoodTrim + MI_WindowGlass.

ENV_Gas_Pipe.method: Natural-gas riser: yellow painted pipe up the facade from a meter box, with clamps.

ENV_Gate_Timber.method: Double-leaf plank gate (warehouse / yard) for the shop/gate opening; kit MI_WoodTrim planks + iron straps.

ENV_Gutter_Channel_2m.method: Central drainage channel for pedestrian streets: two sloped granite slabs forming a shallow V (0.6 m).

ENV_Hill_Tree.method:
Low-cost backdrop tree for the hills around the town: a conifer/oak blob of 2-3 solid painted lobes on a short
trunk, readable in silhouette through the valley fog.

ENV_Intercom.method: Door-entry panel beside a portal (portero automático): aluminium plate, speaker grille, a column of buttons.

ENV_Kerb_2m.method: Granite kerb 2 m x 0.28 m, top at +0.15 (pavement datum); kit MI_RockTrim slab band.

ENV_Kerb_Corner.method: Quarter-round kerb corner (radius 1 m) joining two ENV_Kerb_2m runs; kit MI_RockTrim slab band.

ENV_Kiosk_Plaza.method:
Octagonal plaza kiosk (templete de música): stone base with two steps, eight slim cast-iron columns with
brackets, a frieze, a tiled octagonal roof with a finial. About 7 m across, 6 m high: a landmark for the river
plaza (the real plaza has one) without copying any real building.

ENV_Lamp_Post.method:
Cast-iron street lamp in the classic Spanish 'fernandina' line (about 3.9 m): moulded base, fluted-looking
tapering shaft with collars, four-sided lantern with a pyramid hood and finial.

ENV_Lifebuoy_Post.method: Quay lifebuoy on a post with a small cabinet.

ENV_Manhole.method: Round cast-iron manhole cover flush with the paving.

ENV_Mooring_Line.method: Unit mooring rope along +z (1 m); the assembler stretches it from bollard to boat.

ENV_Net_Pile.method: Heap of fishing net with floats, about 1.4 m wide.

ENV_Pallet.method: Euro pallet 1.2 x 0.8 x 0.14 m; kit MI_WoodTrim dark plank band.

ENV_Parapet_2m.method: Low stone parapet (0.75 m) with granite coping — designed edge for overlooks and terraces.

ENV_Parapet_Rail_2m.method: Stone upstand (0.45 m) with a painted iron rail above it — the public waterfront edge treatment.

ENV_Parapet_Stone_2m.method:
Bridge/river parapet 2 m: masonry body (kit rubble slot, remapped per bridge) under a rounded dressed coping
with drip; 1.0 m high, 0.45 m thick. Local frame: runs along x, centred on z = 0, sits on y = 0.

ENV_Parasol.method: Terrace parasol, 2.4 m canopy; canvas colour is a material slot (ENV_Canvas_Cream).

ENV_Phone_Booth.method: Late-1990s public phone cabin (generic, no branding): grey frame, glass sides, open front.

ENV_Plant_Boxwood.method: Clipped box ball (boj) for a shop door or a formal pot.

ENV_Plant_Geranium.method: Geranio for balcony and window boxes: small round leaves and scattered red flower heads.

ENV_Plant_Hydrangea.method:
Hortensia: the damp-north doorstep and garden shrub — dark leaf mass with big flower balls (blue by default;
the dresser remaps ENV_Flower_Blue to pink or white).

ENV_Plant_Laurel.method: Bay laurel standard in a pot (laurel a la puerta): straight stem and a round clipped head.

ENV_Planter_Box.method: Timber window/doorstep box 0.8 m with soil (flowers placed by the dresser).

ENV_Planter_Pot.method: Terracotta planter pot (0.45 m): foot ring, flared body, rolled rim; soil top. Plants are placed separately.

ENV_Plinth_2m.method:
Ashlar plinth band (zócalo) 2 m x 0.42 m standing 6 cm proud of the wall face: hides the wall/pavement seam
and ties ground floors of different buildings together. Kit MI_RockTrim ashlar band.

ENV_Plinth_Pier.method: Plinth stub for the pier beside a door/shop opening (0.2 m, scaled in x by the assembler).

ENV_Pot_Glazed.method: Glazed ceramic pot (blue by default; remapped to green/ochre): rounded belly, narrow foot, soil.

ENV_Pot_Tin.method: Old olive-oil tin reused as a planter (lata), painted and dented — the modest household touch.

ENV_Puddle_A.method: Irregular rain puddle (flat, glossy), about 1.6 x 1.1 m.

ENV_Puddle_B.method: Irregular rain puddle, about 1.0 x 0.7 m.

ENV_Quay_Ladder.method: Iron ladder fixed to the quay face (top at the coping, 3 m down).

ENV_Quay_Steps.method:
Stone steps running down the quay face to the water (1.6 m drop, 1.2 m wide), outer side wall.
Top step at y = 0 against the coping line (z = 0), descending towards +x.

ENV_Quay_Wall_4m.method: Public quay edge block 4 m long, 3.2 m face down to below water; rubble face + granite coping at y = 0.

ENV_Quoin_Ashlar.method:
Ashlar quoins for one storey (3 m) of an exposed building corner: ten courses alternating long and short
blocks on the two faces, 3 cm proud of the render — slimmer than the kit pilaster the owner rejected. Local frame
as the kit corner piece: the outer corner is at (WALL_FACE, WALL_FACE), faces towards +x and +z.

ENV_Quoin_Slim.method:
Slim quoins for one storey of a seen corner (owner audit 2026-09-29: the ashlar quoins were "repetitivos y
gruesos"): twelve 0.25 m courses of short/long blocks (0.34 / 0.2 m), only 1.2 cm proud, fine arris. Families use
it for dressed-stone corners on rendered houses and, painted, for rendered corner bands.

ENV_Railing_Quay_2m.method: Public waterfront guard rail, 2 m, 1.05 m high: tube posts + three rails (painted iron).

ENV_Recycling_Bins.method: Street recycling set (contenedores): glass (green), packaging (yellow), paper (blue), rounded plastic bodies.

ENV_Retaining_Wall_2x1.method: Retaining wall 2 m long, 1 m face, coping on top (upper datum at y = 0, lower street at -1).

ENV_Retaining_Wall_2x2.method: Retaining wall 2 m long, 2 m face, coping on top.

ENV_Retaining_Wall_2x3.method: Retaining wall 2 m long, 3 m face (one storey), coping on top.

ENV_River_Stairs.method:
Bajada al río: stone steps running down the face of the channel wall from the bank (y = 0) to a landing just
above the water (3 m lower), 1.3 m wide, with an iron handrail on the open side. Runs along +x; the wall face is
at z = 0 and the steps stand in front of it (+z, over the water).

ENV_Roof_Gable_4.method: Plain plaster gable for a 4 m span (roof ends above party walls and gable-fronted sheds).

ENV_Roof_Gable_6.method: Plain plaster gable for a 6 m span (roof ends above party walls and gable-fronted sheds).

ENV_Roof_Gable_8.method: Plain plaster gable for a 8 m span (roof ends above party walls and gable-fronted sheds).

ENV_Sat_Dish.method: Satellite dish on a wall bracket (late-1990s addition), facing +z and up.

ENV_Shop_Fascia.method: Painted fascia board over a shop opening in a moulded timber frame with end consoles (blank board).

ENV_Shopfront_Door.method:
Shop entrance for the shop opening: glazed door leaf (0.95 m) + side light, flush threshold (closed).
New geometry on the kit MI_WoodTrim trim sheet + MI_WindowGlass.

ENV_Shopfront_Door_Open.method:
Same shop entrance with the leaf swung 88 degrees inwards: a walkable 0.9 m public threshold into a shallow
shop interior (the gameplay open/close interaction belongs to later GC2 work).

ENV_Shopfront_Frame.method:
Display window for the shop opening: painted timber frame, stall-riser panel, mullion, transom light.
New geometry on the kit MI_WoodTrim trim sheet + MI_WindowGlass (materials from Window_Wide_Flat1).

ENV_Shutter_Roller.method: Closed metal roller shutter (persiana) filling the shop opening: ribbed curtain, guide rails, housing box.

ENV_Sign_Bracket.method:
Hanging shop sign on a wrought-iron bracket (the Pyrenean/lebaniego street's signature): wall plate, top bar,
a scrolled strut, two rings and a painted board in a moulded dark-timber frame (blank: no lettering in ENV).

ENV_Sign_Direction.method: Pedestrian direction post with two blank arrow plates (typography stays out of ENV).

ENV_Sign_NoEntry.method: Generic no-entry traffic sign on a galvanised post (disc facing +z).

ENV_Sign_Panel.method:
Lettering panel 1 x 1 m (scaled per sign): a 15 mm board whose front face maps one sign texture 0..1. The
district remaps ENV_Sign_Board to the business sign material and scales it to the fascia or wall.

ENV_Slipway.method: Concrete slipway ramp 4 m wide, 7 m long, dropping 1.8 m into the water (+z), stone kerbs.

ENV_Solana_Bay.method:
Solana for one 2 m bay of the top floor (slot frame, y = 0 at the floor): board floor on carved joist tails,
front fascia, balustrade of turned balusters between rails, a post at the bay's left edge rising to the eave with
a zapata. Bays chain along the facade; ENV_Solana_Wing closes the ends. Kit MI_WoodTrim (palette joinery).

ENV_Solana_Wing.method:
Masonry wing wall (cortavientos) closing one end of a solana: 0.3 m thick, as deep as the solana, one storey,
in the building's wall material (MI_Plaster slot, palette remapped) with an ashlar coping. Slot frame at the
facade end; the wing projects along +z.

ENV_Solar_Panel.method: Thermal solar panel with tank on a small frame, for a flat bit of roof or a south slope.

ENV_Stain_Quad.method:
Weathering decal quad 1 x 1 m (x centred, y 0..1) lying 4 mm off the wall face; the dresser picks the stain
cell by material (ENV_Stain_*) and scales it to the cause (a downpipe foot, a sill, a corner, a repair).

ENV_Street_Name_Plate.method: Wall-mounted ceramic street-name plate (blank; the street name is content, not ENV).

ENV_TV_Aerial.method: Rooftop TV aerial: 2.2 m mast with a Yagi boom and elements.

ENV_Telecom_Box.method: Telecom/electric junction box with the cable dropping into it.

ENV_Threshold_Slab.method: Flush stone slab in front of a shop or portal (walkable, 2 cm proud with a chamfer).

ENV_Trash_Bags.method: Three tied rubbish bags left by a door or bin.

ENV_Tree_Pit.method: Square iron tree-pit grate (alcorque) 1.3 m with a trunk hole.

ENV_Tree_Plaza.method:
Plaza tree (plane/lime, pollarded): tapering trunk with bark (Nature pack bark), three limbs and a solid
painted crown of clustered lobes — no alpha cards (owner: card crowns read as big cards).

ENV_Tree_Singular.method:
The old plane tree of the plaza (árbol singular): thick buttressed trunk, big limbs, a wide high crown, and
a round stone bench around it — the second 'I am here' of the plaza, the shade where the old men sit.

ENV_Trough_Stone.method: Old stone trough (pila) reused as a planter by a house door.

ENV_Utility_Box.method:
Meter cabinet (hornacina de contadores) on a ground-floor facade: galvanised steel box with a recessed door,
hinges, lock, louvres and the service conduit down to the ground.

ENV_Vehicle_Car.method: Small 1990s hatchback (generic), 3.7 m, front towards +z. Body paint slot ENV_Paint_Red.

ENV_Vehicle_Van.method: Small 1990s delivery van (generic, no branding), 4.1 m, front towards +z. Body paint slot ENV_Paint_White.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean.method: Plain plaster bay without half-timbering: keeps only the floor-line band.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean_Base.method: Ground-floor plaster bay with the kit brick plinth kept, sill band/timber removed.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean_Door.method: Plaster bay with the flat door opening (portals, balcony doors); side sill bands removed.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean_DoorRound.method: Plaster bay with the arched door opening; timber removed.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean_Thin.method: Plaster bay with the small round-head window; timber removed.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Clean_Window.method: Plaster bay with the wide window opening; sill band removed, brick spandrel rendered over.

ENV_Wall_Plaster_Shopfront.method: Clean plaster ground-floor wall with a 1.6 x 2.38 m shop opening cut by boolean; reveals in kit stone trim.

ENV_Wall_UnevenBrick_Shopfront.method: Kit rubble-stone wall with the same shop/gate opening; reveals in kit stone trim.

ENV_Water_Plane_20m.method: Port water surface tile 20 x 20 m (y = 0 is the water level; place it below the quay coping).

ENV_Weathervane.method: Iron weathervane: rod, cardinal cross and an arrow with a cockerel-less swallowtail vane.

ENV_Window_Blind.method:
Retro-fitted PVC roller blind (persiana enrollable) for the kit wide window: box over the head, slats
lowered two thirds — the typical 1970s–90s replacement over older joinery.

ENV_Window_Boarded.method: Boarded-up window for neglected buildings: rough planks across the kit wide window (MI_WoodTrim dark).

ENV_Window_Insert_Thin.method:
Glazed insert for the kit rubble-stone round-head window (±0.32 m, springing 2.31 m, crown 2.51 m):
rectangular sash plus a segmental glass head.

ENV_Window_Insert_Wide.method:
Glazed joinery insert for the kit rubble-stone wide window opening (±0.60 x 1.05–2.31 m, measured on the
donor wall). The kit's `Window_Wide_Flat_Rocks` is only a stone surround; without this the building's empty
interior shows through. Recessed behind the surround: frame, mullion, transom, glass.

ENV_Window_Wide_Ashlar.method:
Wide window for rendered walls in the casco manner: sandstone surround (jambs in alternating blocks, lintel
with ears, projecting sill) around the kit opening (±0.6, 1.05-2.31) and a recessed glazed sash. Replaces the
kit's white timber trim window where the grammar asks for ashlar surrounds.
